items.title: Serre's vanishing theorem for Galois cohomology under the vanishing of Brauer groups
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition, attributed by the author to Serre, deduces the vanishing of Galois cohomology from the vanishing of the Brauer groups of all finite extensions of K: H^q(Gal(K^sep/K), (K^sep)^*) = 0 for q at least 1 and H^q(Gal, M) = 0 for torsion M and q at least 2 (statement lines 10693-10707, whose commented reference block is excluded from the counted spans as explained in the notes). The proof proceeds by translating to etale cohomology of Spec(K) (proof lines 10709-10729), then splits according to whether the prime l under consideration differs from or equals char(K): the Kummer sequence together with the hypothesis on Brauer groups and dimension shifting handles the first case (proof lines 10732-10755), the Artin-Schreier sequence handles the second (proof lines 10758-10776), and assertion (1) requires a further argument comparing the multiplicative group with its divisible part (proof lines 10779-10794). The non-formal content is the organisation of the two characteristic cases and the final dimension argument. The claim is H2: a complete author proof with three separate steps, each written out.
